title: Gilad and the Neighbor's Donkey
summary: Gilad finds a lost donkey in the field and discovers it belongs to the grumpy neighbor who always shouts at the children. He remembers what Grandpa taught him from the Torah, to return a lost thing even to someone you don't get along with, and brings the donkey home. A story about returning lost things, doing what is right, and a new friendship.
pages:
Gilad lives in a small village, with green fields and a chicken coop.
What he loves most is running through the field in his straw hat.

One day, in the middle of the field, he heard: "Hee-haw! Hee-haw!"
Behind a bush stood a gray donkey with long ears, looking completely lost.

"Whose are you, donkey?" asked Gilad.
Around the donkey's neck hung a bell, and on it was written: "Shimon."

"Oh," sighed Gilad. "Shimon the neighbor."
Shimon is the neighbor who always shouts, "Quiet, children!"
And once Gilad's ball fell into his yard, and Shimon didn't give it back.

"Maybe I'll just leave him here," thought Gilad.
"Shimon wasn't nice to me. Why should I be nice to him?"

Then Gilad remembered what Grandpa had read to him from the Torah on Shabbat:
"When you find a donkey that has wandered off, bring it back to its owner. Even if you quarrel, even if you aren't friends."

"It's not the donkey's fault that we quarrel," said Gilad.
"And he must be hungry, and missing home."
He gently took hold of the rope and said, "Come on, donkey. We're going home."

The way was long, and the donkey was stubborn.
Once he stopped to eat a flower, and once he sat down in the middle of the path.
"Come on, donkey!" Gilad laughed.

Gilad knocked on Shimon's gate.
Shimon opened it with a sour face, and then he saw the donkey.
"My Balbo!" he shouted. "I've been looking for you all morning!"

Shimon hugged the donkey, and then he looked at Gilad.
"You brought him? All that way?"
Gilad nodded.

Shimon went into the house and came back with something in his hand: Gilad's ball!
"Sorry I didn't give it back to you," he said quietly. "I was grumpy."

Since then, every Friday, Gilad and Shimon feed Balbo carrots together.
And when the ball falls into the yard? Shimon throws it right back, with a smile.

Have you ever found something that someone lost?
Returning a lost thing is the right thing to do, even for someone who isn't so nice to us.
And sometimes, that's exactly how a new friendship begins.
